(R1-Ex-parte)
R2-By Gururaj Salur, Advocate)
JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 01-07-2022 at about 2.00 p.m., the petitioner was riding TVS moped bearing No.KA-02-EC- 5468 from Madakashira Town to his Native place.

When he reached in front of Dhall Mill on Madakashira to Madhugiri town, at that time the rider of Hero HF Deluxe Motorcycle bearing Reg.no.AP-39-GP-8119 came at high speed in a rash and negligent manner , dashed against the petitioner's TVS moped result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.

Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Madakashira wherein first aid treatment was taken and then shifted to Raghavendra People Tree Hospitals, and Bangalore wherein he was admitted as an inpatient from 02-07-2022 to 08-07-2022.

entities.text: Raghavendra People Tree Hospitals, and Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Again the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient in the same hospital from 28-07- 2022 to 30-07-2022.
The petitioner was advised to continue medicines and follow up treatment.
So far the petitioner has spent Rs.2, 00,000/- towards hospitalization charges and incidental expenses.
The petitioner has to undergo further surgery for removal of implants and incurred huge expenses for future treatment and medical expenses.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
The petitioner was aged about 50 years and he was doing business and thereby earning sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability petitioner is not in a position to do the said work.
He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of income, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
3. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent hence he was placed ex-parte.

4. Respondent No.2- The ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co.Ltd.,/insurer of the Hero HF Deluxe Motorcycle bearing No.AP-39-GP-8119 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
It is contended that the insured vehicle was not at all involved in the alleged accident and same has been implicated in order to get wrongful gain and to make wrongful loss to the Insurance Company.
It is further contended that the rider of the insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving, that there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the insured vehicle.

Narasappa .G vs Rangappa on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49556567/
2 5.

On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves
that ,

he had sustained grievous injuries in the RTA alleged to have occurred on 01-07-2022 at about 02.00 P.M., in front of Dhall Mill on Madakasira to Madhugiri Town, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of Hero HF Deluxe motorcycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39- GP-8119?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum?
From whom payable?

3. What Order or Award?
6.
The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and examined one witness as P.W.2 and marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P12 and closed evidence on his side.

On the other hand, M.Shivakumar -Deputy Civil Surgeon at District Hospital, Hindupur is examined as RW.1 and got marked copy of MLC as Ex.R1.
7.
Heard arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.
Issue No.1 : -

In order to explain the actionable negligence of the rider of offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that was occurred on the stated date when the petitioner was riding TVS moped bearing No.KA-02-EC- 5468 from Madakashira Town to his Native place and when he reached in front of Dhall Mill on Madakashira to Madhugiri town, at that time the rider of Hero HF Deluxe Motorcycle bearing Reg.no.AP-39-GP-8119 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came at high speed in rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner's TVS moped result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained,
treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
10.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 5 which are the police records such as compliant copy in telugu version, translated copy of Ex.P.1, F.I.R, Charge sheet, spot mahazar in telugu version, translated copy of Ex.P.4, IMV report are the material documents to prove the present issue.

Narasappa .G vs Rangappa on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49556567/
3 11.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by M.G.Mohan Kumar, case has been registered against the rider of offending vehicle in Crime No.105/2022 of Madakasira Police Station for the offence punishable under section 337 of IPC.
After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 338 of IPC.
12. The respondent no.2 has disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident and has argued much regarding the delay of 6 days in lodging the complaint.

13. At the cost of repetition it is the case of the petitioner that on the date of accident he was proceeding in his TVS moped bearing No.KA-02-EC-5468 and offending vehicle which came from the same road hit against his motorcycle and thereby submitted that there are two vehicles involved in the accident.
The petitioner has produced the spot mahazar but has not produced the site plan.
It is not in dispute that the accident in question has occurred in the road.

If the discharge summary issued by the People Tree Hospital, admission record and assessment summary which are in the case sheet is perused, wherein the history of injury is mentioned as "pedestrian hit by two wheeler".

If the medical documents are perused, soon after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Madhakasira and on the same date he was shifted to Raghavendra People Tree Hospitals at Bangalore.

entities.text: Raghavendra People Tree Hospitals at Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In all the medical records the history of injury is mentioned as "Pedestrian hit by two wheeler" and nowhere in the medical records the involvement of two vehicles is mentioned.
If really the petitioner was riding the TVS Moped , the said fact would have been mentioned in the MLC and in the other medical records.
Further as observed supra though the accident in question has occurred on 01-07-2022 but complaint came to be lodged on 06-07-2022.
In the complaint the involvement of two vehicles are mentioned and there is mention that the offending vehicle hit against the right side footboard of the vehicle of the petitioner.
If the spot mahazar is perused, it was drawn on 07-07-2022.
In the spot mahazar there is clear mention about the occurrence of the accident in the road.

Though the spot mahazar was drawn on 07-07-2022 i.e.,
after lapse of nearly 7 days from the date of accident but in the spot mahazar it is stated that at the time of drawing the spot mahazar, the two vehicles allegedly involved in the accident were lying in the spot and both the vehicles were seized under the mahazar.

When accident has occurred in a public place, it is highly unbelievable to say that even after 7 days of the accident the said vehicles were in the spot itself without its being shifted to some other place so as to facilitate the free movement of other vehicles passing through the said road .

Though it is stated that both the vehicles were seized under mahazar and though in the complaint it is stated that the offending vehicle is hit against the right foot step of the alleged TVS moped but very strangely the alleged TVS moped of the petitioner was not subject to IMV inspection.
If Ex.P5 is perused, only offending vehicle was inspected by the RTO and in the Ex.P5 it is reported that no damages was found in the offending vehicle.

If really the offending vehicle was hit against the TVS moped of the petitioner then definite some amount of damages would have been caused both to the offending vehicle and moped but no damage was found on the offending vehicle.

Hence, it clearly reveals that the offending vehicle was hit against the petitioner who was the pedestrian passing in the road but not against the alleged TVS moped and alleged TVS moped was not at all involved in the accident.
So far as the dispute raised as to the involvement of offending vehicle is concerned, in all the medical records including MLC there is clear mention about the two wheeler hit against the pedestrian.

Hence, involvement of two Narasappa .G vs Rangappa on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49556567/
4 wheeler/ offending vehicle in the accident cannot be ruled out.

14. From the materials it can be gathered the petitioner who as pedestrian while walking on the road met with an accident and by walking on the public road instead in the foot path without taking precautionary measures of vehicles plying in the said road , he too has contributed some amount of negligence.

Hence, the negligence contributed by the petitioner can be assessed at the ratio of 15%
and of the offending vehicle at the ratio of 85% and the petitioner has to forgo compensation to the extent of negligence contributed by him.
Hence, issue No.1 is answered in the partly affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summary which are marked at Ex.P.6, and Ex.P7.

On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken primary treatment at Andhra Pradesh Vaidya Vidhana Parishad Community Centre and then he has taken treatment as inpatient at People Tree Hospital, for three times, first time from 01-07-2022 to 02-07-2022 , second time from 02-07-2022 to 08-07-2022 and third time from 28-07-2022 to 30-07-2022 in all for a period of 11 days.

entities.text: Andhra Pradesh Vaidya Vidhana Parishad Community Centre
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained three injuries which are grievous in nature.

16. Dr. Nagaraj B N - Orthopedic surgeon and legal consultant at People Tree Hospital is examined as Pw2 and through him recent examination report, case sheets and recent X-ray film are got marked as per Ex.
. P.W.2 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 05- 03-2024 clinically, radiological for assessment of disability.
The PW.2 further deposed that petitioner has suffered physical disability to the right lower limb at 66% and to the whole body at 22%.

PW.2 further deposed that the petitioner needs another surgery the approximate cost of the surgery would be around Rs.40, 000/- per month.
17.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
18. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained three grievous injuries.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.65,000/- towards pain and suffering.
19. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, the petitioner has produced 80 medical bills for Rs.68,916/- as per Ex.P.8.
If the medical documents are perused, the petitioner has incurred net medical bill of Rs.2,32,847/-, out of which Rs.2,14,763 /- is reimbursed under Medi Assist India Pvt Ltd., .
As per the receipt and as per the final bill the petitioner has paid only sum of Rs.18,084/-.
The petitioner has produced some medical bills of which medical bills for Rs.130/-, for Rs.390/-, Rs.600/-, Rs.570/- Rs.513/- and Rs.318/- are Xerox copies without any seal of the hospital pharmacy.
Hence, out of Rs.68,915/-, sum of Rs.2,521/- has to be deducted and on such deduction the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner would come to Rs Rs.66,394/- .

Narasappa .G vs Rangappa on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49556567/
5 20.

The learned counsel for respondent no.2 has referred judgment rendered in MFA No.789/2016 (MV) between Mohankumar T Vs. Reliance General Insurance Co.Ltd., wherein it is observed that "
Whatever the amount reimbursed by any Health scheme/Insurer that as to be deducted from the total medical bills and only the medical bill amount paid by the patient has to be considered.

entities.text: Mohankumar T Vs. Reliance General Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case the petitioner has claimed medical bill amount only to the extent of patient share paid by them.

It is true that in the said medical bills as referred above some are Xerox copies and after deducting the amount mentioned in the Xerox copies of the medical bill, by considering the rest of the medical bills, compensation to the tune of Rs.66,394/- is paid under the head medical expenses.
21.
It is stated that petitioner was aged about 50 years and he was doing Tamarind business and thereby earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
But to substantiate the said contention petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence considering the age, the year of accident and the place of residence this court inclines to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,500/- p.m.
22.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and taken treatment for 11 days as inpatient in Raghavendra People Tree Hospital, Bengaluru.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of two months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.15,500/- p.m. for two months.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.31,000/- towards loss of income during the laid down period .
23. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at People Tree Hospital.
Further for 11 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.25,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2022.
24. The PW.2 has assessed the disability of petitioner on the right lower limb at 66% and to the whole body physical disability at 22%.

25. If the evidence of PW.2 is perused, it is admitted by PW.2 that if correction surgery is made there may be possibility of reducing the percentage of disability and that if injured required future surgery under such circumstances, the permanent disability of the injured cannot be assessed.
Hence, it can be said that the disability of petitioner is not correctly assessed by the Pw2 and he has assessed the disability of petitioner on higher side.
Hence considering the said fact this court inclines to consider the disability of petitioner at 15%, as petitioner is stated to be a Tamarind business man.
26. It is stated by the petitioner that at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 50 years.

In this regard, the petitioner has produced Aadhaar card/Ex.P.9 of the petitioner which shows his date of birth as 01-01- 1971 and as the accident in question took place in the year 2022, therefore the deceased was aged about 51 years as on the date of accident.

Narasappa .G vs Rangappa on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49556567/
6 27.

So taking in to consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.15,500/- p.m , if 15% of loss of earning capacity is considered and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 51 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 51 to 55 is '11'.
So by applying the multiplier '11' the future loss of income due to disability comes to Rs.2,45,520/-.
Hence this Tribunal holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,06,900/- (i.e., 15,500 x15% x 11 x12 ) towards future loss of income due to disability.
28. As per the evidence of Pw2, the petitioner needs another surgery the estimate cost of the surgery is Rs.40,000/-.
But admittedly PW.2 has not given estimation.

Hence, this court inclines to award future medical expenses only to the tune of Rs.15,000/-.
30.
The petitioner at this advanced age has suffered three injuries, hence he may suffer loss of amenities and discomfort.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under the head loss of amenities and discomfort.

Thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
Sl.N Heads Amount o.
1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 65,000/-

2 . Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 25,000/-
 charges and nourishing food 3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 31,000/-
 laid up period 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 66,394/-
5. Loss of future income Rs.3,06,900/-
6.

Future medical expenses Rs. 15,000/-
7. Loss of amenities and discomfort Rs. 30,000/-

Therefore, this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.5,39,294/- (Rupees Five Lakh Thirty Nine Thousand Two Hundred Ninety Four only).
31.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Since both petitioner and respondent no.2 had contributed negligence to the extent of 15:85 this court has already come to the conclusion that out of the total compensation amount, petitioner has to forgo compensation to an extent of 15%.
The respondent no 2 being the insurer is liable to pay 85% of the awarded compensation to the petitioners.

85% of the compensation shall carry interest at 6 % p.a.
accordingly issue no 2 is answered.
32. Issue No.3: In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

Narasappa .G vs Rangappa on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49556567/
7
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation Rs.5,39,294/- (Rupees Five Lakh Thirty Nine Thousand Two Hundred Ninety Four only).

The Respondent No 2 is liable to pay 85% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.4,58,400/- +
cost of Rs 1,000/- on IA, in all sum of Rs.4,59,400/- (Rupees Four Lakh Fifty Eight Thousand Four Hundred only) with interest on sum of Rs.4,43,400/- at 6% within 2 months from the date of this award.
It shall also carry interest at 6% per annum on Rs.4,43,400/- from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Petitioner shall forgo 15% of the compensation amount i.e., to the extent of Rs.80,894/-.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner through E- payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 8 th day of October 2024.)
(ROOPASHRI) XXII Addl. SCJ & ACJM Bengaluru.
